item.title: Cops have to treat marijuana in your car differently after new California Supreme Court ruling
item.description: If you can't easily consume it, having marijuana in your car does not give California police the right to search the vehicle.

item.title: California chief justice steps up monitoring of immigration arrests at courthouses
item.description: California's top judge wants to deter immigration agents from making arrests in courthouses, a practice that she says instills fear in witnesses and litigants.

item.title: Coalition seeks LA County sales tax vote to offset federal healthcare funding cuts
item.description: A newly formed coalition wants to bring a half-cent sales tax before Angeleno voters in June to mitigate Medi-Cal losses

item.title: California neglects its private duty nurses and fails its sick children
item.description: Hundreds of California children are stuck in hospitals because their families wait months or years for private nursing care they’re legally entitled to.

item.title: San Diego teachers plan first strike in 30 years over issues with staffing and services for special education
item.description: San Diego teachers plan their first strike in 30 years on Feb. 26, accusing the district of failing to meet special education staffing standards and shortchanging services for students with disabilities.

item.title: Matt Mahan’s campaign for California governor will be a voter litmus test
item.description: With San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, a moderate Democrat, entering the governor's race, the outcome will help reveal just how liberal California truly is.

item.title: ‘We’re basically pushers:’ Two California courtrooms hear how companies may have hooked kids on social media
item.description: Lawsuits in California federal and state court are unearthing documents embarrassing to tech companies — and may be a tipping point into federal regulation.

item.title: San Diego journalist fighting prostate cancer warns: ‘This could happen to you, too’
item.description: Jerry McCormick’s path to recover from prostate cancer has been anything but linear. Documenting progress and setbacks helps him find purpose.

item.title: Black men in California face higher risks and higher bills for prostate cancer
item.description: Black Californians are five times more likely than others to die of prostate cancer. Gov. Gavin Newsom vetoed a bill that would have cut screening costs.
